items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Well, at that time, Roosevelt came in with the Blue Eagle thing.

ctx.x: of money so you could retire. You're talking pre-Roosevelt so you're not talking Social Security.

Now, one of the funniest things there was Totts Scott, a piano player and a very fine one. Well, at that time, Roosevelt came in with the Blue Eagle thing. Now, that we should not be unfair to labor and all that. And the Liberty Inn was not that organized, anyway. They were very much against it. And one night, Tut got out -- whatever Rosicrucian or Far Eastern kick he was on, and decided to make a speech. And he told the drummer, give me a roll of the drums.

The drummer gave him a roll, and he upped and made this speech. And one of the help got Johnny McGovern, who was a tough Irish kid. And we're standing there listening to this guy talk, telling the people not to come in and go away, they were unfair and all that. And he's ready to kill this guy. And McGovern says, don't kill him, shake him. I never seen anything like that. He picked Tut up and just shook him, and shook all that nonsense out of him.
